activity.notes: Martin Luther's Reformation activity is represented from 1517, when he published the Ninety-Five Theses at Wittenberg, through his death in 1546. Wittenberg and Luther's principal teaching and reform work lay in the Electorate of Saxony, whose ruler Frederick the Wise later protected him. ATLAS records religious activity rather than governance and does not confuse him with Martin Luther King Jr.

sources.title: Martin Luther — Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy
sources.citation_text: The Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy identifies Luther's 1517 Ninety-Five Theses as the beginning of the impact that became the Reformation, records his long professorship at Wittenberg, and follows his activity through his death in 1546.
